DIAGNOSIS READY: Cocaine-induced Parkinsonism.

The combination of long-term heavy cocaine use, recent cessation, and the specific triad of psychiatric symptoms (hallucinations, irritability), autonomic/motor changes (swallowing difficulty, tremor), and cognitive decline strongly points to toxic-metabolic encephalopathy from cocaine rather than primary neurodegenerative or autoimmune disorders.
